		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">ITEM 1. BUSINES<a name="ITEM1BUSINESS_552802"></a>S&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company devoted to providing transformative therapies to people bravely facing cancer.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our primary focus is to develop treatments for solid tumors using various approaches, including small molecules and immuno-oncology antibodies, as monotherapies or in combinations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have in-licensed and are developing several oncology-related product candidates, and we have entered into several research collaborations with third parties for the discovery of new candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have also entered into arrangements with other companies for the development and commercialization of certain of our product candidates in specific indications and/or geographies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">To date, we have received regulatory approvals for the following products, which are currently marketed and sold in the U.S. and in certain countries in Europe:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:9pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, or FDA, approved ZEJULA&#xAE; (niraparib) in March 2017 for the maintenance treatment of women with recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer who are in a complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The European Commission, or EC, approved ZEJULA in November 2017 as a monotherapy for the maintenance treatment of adult patients with platinum-sensitive relapsed high grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer who&nbsp;are in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt;">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:9pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">VARUBI&#xAE; (rolapitant) is a potent and long-acting neurokinin-1, or NK-1, receptor antagonist for the prevention of chemotherapy induced nausea and vomiting, or CINV.&nbsp; &nbsp;The FDA approved VARUBI in oral formulation in September 2015 for use in combination with other antiemetic agents in adults for the prevention of delayed (24 to 120 hours after chemotherapy administration) nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of emetogenic cancer chemotherapy, including, but not limited to, highly emetogenic chemotherapy. &nbsp;The EC approved VARUBY&#xAE;, the brand name of oral rolapitant in Europe, in April 2017 for the prevention of delayed nausea and vomiting associated with highly and moderately emetogenic chemotherapy in adults.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA approved the intravenous, or IV, formulation of VARUBI in October 2017.&nbsp; In January 2018, after post-marketing reports of side effects experienced following the commercial introduction of VARUBI IV, we updated the VARUBI IV package insert, including modifications to the contraindications, warnings and precautions, and adverse reactions sections, and issued a &#x201C;Dear Healthcare Professional Letter&#x201D; to healthcare providers to highlight the updates. &nbsp;In February 2018, we determined that we would cease marketing and distribution of VARUBI IV and pursue strategic alternatives for the VARUBI brand, including potentially out-licensing the VARUBI product line.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Development Programs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Niraparib</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Niraparib is an orally active and potent poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase, or PARP, inhibitor.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on research related to PARP inhibitors generally, we believe niraparib may also be active in the treatment of several tumor types.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are conducting several ongoing clinical trials evaluating niraparib for the treatment of various tumor types, as a monotherapy and in combination with other therapeutics, including our own immuno-oncology assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect to initiate additional clinical trials of niraparib during 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are also collaborating with various other organizations to evaluate niraparib in combination with other therapeutics for the treatment of various cancers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Immuno-Oncology</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Pursuant to our collaboration and exclusive license agreement with AnaptysBio, Inc., or AnaptysBio, we are developing several antibodies for immuno-oncology targets.&nbsp; The antibodies and related development activities are summarized as follows:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">TSR-042 (anti-PD-1): We initiated a Phase 1, dose escalation study of TSR-042 in March 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have also initiated expansion cohorts in patients with advanced solid tumors, including non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC, endometrial cancer and metastatic microsatellite instability-high, or MSI-H, tumors.&nbsp;&nbsp;We plan to pursue an accelerated registration path for TSR-042 in metastatic MSI-H tumors.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In addition, we are evaluating our immuno-oncology anti-tumor agents in combination studies with niraparib and other anti-tumor agents.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have also entered into agreements with other third parties for the discovery of other potential oncology product candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to potential candidates arising from such agreements, we intend to continue to leverage the experience and competencies of our senior management team to identify, acquire, develop and commercialize cancer therapeutics, including those that are potentially safer and more effective than existing treatments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Upon successful development and regulatory approval of any of our product candidates, we intend to pursue commercialization of them in key product markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;At this time, we intend to focus on commercializing our products directly in North America and Europe, and in partnership with established companies in other key markets.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Our Strategy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Our strategy is to leverage the experience and competencies of our management team to identify, acquire and develop promising drug candidates and to commercialize cancer therapeutics that are potentially improvements over existing treatments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Key components of our strategy include:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Continue the Clinical Development of and Successfully Commercialize Niraparib for the Treatment of Cancers that are Susceptible to PARP Inhibition.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;We are evaluating niraparib in several clinical trials in ovarian cancer with the goal of expanding the currently approved indication, and in other cancers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We plan to initiate further clinical trials during 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are also evaluating niraparib in combination studies with our immuno-oncology anti-tumor agents, and with other therapeutics.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Advance Potential Immuno-Oncology Antibody Product Candidates.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;Under our collaboration and exclusive license agreement with AnaptysBio, we received exclusive rights to monospecific antibody product candidates targeting PD-1, TIM-3 and LAG-3, and certain bi-specific antibody product candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have clinical trials ongoing for each monospecific antibody, as monotherapies and in combinations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have initiated pre-clinical research for TSR-075, our bi-specific anti-PD-1/LAG-3 candidate.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we are evaluating our immuno-oncology candidates in combination studies with niraparib and other anti-tumor agents.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">In-license or Acquire Additional Product Candidates to Create a Balanced Product Portfolio.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;We intend to in-license or acquire additional product candidates across various stages of development.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we do not have, nor do we intend to establish, our own drug discovery capabilities, we have entered into multiple research collaborations for the discovery of new product candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;We intend to focus on product candidates that we believe are differentiated from existing cancer therapeutics and that have well-defined, and potentially expeditious, clinical and regulatory pathways.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our objective is to build a portfolio of cancer therapeutics that is balanced by stage of development, resource requirements and development risk.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 72pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Build Global Capabilities to Maximize the Value of Our Product Candidates.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp; &nbsp;We have obtained exclusive worldwide rights to all of our current product candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;We intend for our product candidates to be developed and commercialized globally, by us in key markets and in collaboration with other companies for other geographies.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are collaborating with other companies with regard to selected indications or geographical areas for our in-licensed product candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;We will also seek to acquire global rights for product candidates we acquire or in-license in the future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">6</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Overview of the Market for Cancer Therapeutics and Oncology Supportive Care Products</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells.&nbsp;&nbsp;In January 2018, the American Cancer Society projected that there will be an estimated 1.7 million new cancer cases diagnosed and 609,640 cancer deaths in the United States in 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;Current treatments for cancer include surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, hormone therapy, targeted therapy and immunotherapy.&nbsp;&nbsp;The IQVIA Institute for Human Data Science reported in 2017 that total global spending on oncology medicines, including therapeutic treatments and supportive care, reached $113 billion in 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Many marketed products and product candidates for treating cancer patients that are currently being developed by biopharmaceutical companies are cytotoxic chemotherapies that exert their anti-tumor effect on cancer generally through nonspecific damage to cellular components with the goal of causing cancer cell malfunction and cell death.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other products and product candidates alter cell metabolism or internal repair mechanisms leading to the demise of the cancer cell.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">More recently, targeted anti-cancer agents have been designed by scientists to inhibit the action of specific molecules within cancer cells that are driving the aberrant growth responsible for tumor development.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of these targeted agents are developed in conjunction with companion diagnostic tests that are used by clinicians to determine if a patient&#x2019;s cancerous tumor contains these specific molecules and is, therefore, more likely to respond to a particular targeted therapy.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recent advances in cancer immunology have led to the development and availability of effective immunotherapies for the treatment of certain cancers.&nbsp; We have acquired product candidates for which we believe diagnostics or specific clinical criteria may allow us to identify cancer patients who will be more likely to be responsive to treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the future, our preference will be to in-license or acquire cancer therapeutics that can be developed in a targeted patient population selected for those who may respond to the drug candidate.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect that the characteristics of these compounds will permit us to design clinical trials that, if successful, may allow us to achieve clinical outcomes that will support regulatory approval for targeted patient groups and reimbursement by healthcare payors due to attractive risk/benefit metrics in the targeted population.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Treatment centers (such as hospitals and community cancer centers) and the healthcare professionals who treat cancer patients (physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, nurses and pharmacists) utilize various combinations of cancer therapeutics and oncology supportive care products to extend and improve the quality of life of these patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">All of these approaches may be associated with various side effects experienced by cancer patients that result from the treatments having an adverse impact on normal functioning cells and organ systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;Some of the more common side effects of cancer therapy include nausea, vomiting or emesis, infections, fatigue and diarrhea.&nbsp;&nbsp;Supportive care products are frequently prescribed or administered to cancer patients to prevent or treat these side effects thereby allowing the patients to continue to receive potentially life prolonging cancer therapies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Our strategy is aligned with these trends in cancer care; that is, to acquire, in-license and develop product candidates and to commercialize products that selectively treat cancers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Our Product Candidates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Niraparib</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Key Characteristics of Niraparib</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Based on nonclinical and clinical data, we believe niraparib may have advantages as a treatment for certain cancers, including:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">niraparib concentrations are higher in the tumor relative to plasma, deliver potent inhibition of PARP and demonstrated tumor growth inhibition in tumor models;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">favorable pharmacokinetic properties in humans;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">reduction of PARP activity in human subjects;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">dosage formulation amenable to further clinical and commercial development;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">7</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">clinical activity with once daily oral administration as a monotherapy; and</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 18pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">tolerability in a Phase 1 combination trial with full doses of another chemotherapy agent, temozolomide, and a biologically active dose of niraparib.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Based upon these key characteristics, we believe that niraparib has the potential to be effective in patients with several tumor types.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Immuno-Oncology</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Background</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Antibodies to immune checkpoint receptors have demonstrated promise in the treatment of tumors, including metastatic melanoma, renal cell carcinoma and NSCLC.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the normal function of immune checkpoint receptors is to maintain immune homeostasis, they are co-opted by certain tumors to evade immune surveillance.&nbsp;&nbsp;PD-1, TIM-3 and LAG-3 are each checkpoint regulators that modulate the function of the immune system via different mechanisms and, when activated and interacting with their respective ligands, may limit the ability of the immune system to respond effectively to tumors.&nbsp;&nbsp;By blocking the interaction of PD-1, TIM-3 and LAG-3 with their respective ligands, antibodies targeting these checkpoint regulators aim to restore immune anti-cancer function in patients across a variety of tumor types.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that therapeutic antibodies selected from our collaboration with AnaptysBio could form the basis of a strategic platform that will potentially enable us to develop novel monotherapy and combination-based approaches with immuno-oncology and other anti-cancer agents in a variety of new tumor indications, both with our existing product candidates and potentially with new candidates we either in-license or access through collaborative transactions with others.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Anti-PD-1 Antibodies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1, CD279) is a well-validated target for tumor immunotherapy.&nbsp;&nbsp;PD-1 operates as a negative regulator of T-cell function and interacts with two ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many tumor types up-regulate PD-L1 on the cell surface as a means of modulating the host immune system and avoiding anti-tumor responses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Antibodies to PD-1 have now been studied in a number of clinical trials in several tumor types.&nbsp;&nbsp;Anti-tumor responses of long duration have been noted, which may be further promoted through combination therapy with additional immuno-regulatory therapeutics.&nbsp;&nbsp;Anti-PD-1 antibodies are now approved in multiple tumor types including, but not limited to, melanoma, NSCLC, bladder and renal carcinoma.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Anti-TIM-3 Antibodies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">T-cell immunoglobulin domain and mucin domain-3 (TIM-3), initially identified on activated Th1 cells, has been shown to be a negative regulator of the immune response.&nbsp;&nbsp;Blockade of TIM-3 promotes T-cell mediated anti-tumor immunity and has anti-tumor activity in a range of mouse tumor models.&nbsp;&nbsp;Combinations of TIM-3 blockade with other immunotherapeutic agents such as TSR-042, anti-CD137 antibodies and others, can be additive or synergistic in increasing anti-tumor effects.&nbsp;&nbsp;TIM-3 expression has been associated with a number of different tumor types, including melanoma, NSCLC and renal cancer, and additionally, expression of intratumoral TIM-3 has been shown to correlate with poor prognosis across a range of tumor types, including NSCLC, cervical, and gastric cancers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Blockade of TIM-3 is also of interest in promoting increased immunity to a number of chronic viral diseases.&nbsp;&nbsp;TIM-3 has also been shown to interact with a number of ligands, including galectin-9, phosphatidylserine and HMGB1, although which of these, if any, are relevant in regulation of anti-tumor responses is not clear at present.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Anti-LAG-3 and Bi-Specific Anti-PD-1/LAG-3 Antibodies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Lymphocyte-activation gene-3 (LAG-3) is a CD4-related transmembrane protein expressed on activated T-cells and regulatory T-cells.&nbsp;&nbsp;Following T-cell activation and up-regulation of LAG-3, LAG-3 binds major histocompatibility complex, or MHC, class II molecules and results in down-regulation of the immune response.&nbsp;&nbsp;Affinity of LAG-3 for MHC class II is higher than that of CD4, allowing for potent dampening of T-cell activation via direct blocking of the interaction as well as direct signaling.&nbsp;&nbsp;Blockade of LAG-3 promotes T-cell mediated anti-tumor immunity and has anti-tumor activity in a range of mouse tumor models.&nbsp;&nbsp;Simultaneous blockade of LAG-3 with PD-1 appears to be synergistic with enhanced anti-tumor effects.&nbsp; In addition, we have selected a bi-specific antibody to PD-1 and LAG-3 as a potential clinical candidate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">8</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

We are responsible for all activities necessary to develop and commercialize niraparib.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In March 2014, we entered into a collaboration and exclusive license agreement with AnaptysBio, a therapeutic antibody company.&nbsp;&nbsp;We executed an amendment in November 2014 to add an additional bi-specific antibody product candidate.&nbsp;&nbsp;We entered into another amendment in February 2016 to extend the term of the initial discovery period and our and AnaptysBio&#x2019;s associated activities under the agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the terms of the agreement, we possess an exclusive, royalty-bearing, sublicensable worldwide license to research, develop, manufacture, market and sell products based on AnaptysBio&#x2019;s proprietary technology for the discovery, generation and optimization of certain specified immunotherapy antibodies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, we received exclusive rights to monospecific antibody product candidates targeting PD-1 (TSR-042), TIM-3 (TSR-022), LAG-3 (TSR-033) and certain bi-specific antibody product candidates, including TSR-075, a bi-specific anti-PD-1/LAG-3 candidate.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the agreement, AnaptysBio was responsible for performing initial discovery and development of therapeutic antibodies against immune checkpoint proteins, with the goal of generating immunotherapy antibodies for use in </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">While we believe that our development experience and scientific knowledge provide us with competitive advantages, our industry is highly competitive and subject to rapid and significant technological change.&nbsp;&nbsp;Compared to TESARO, many of our competitors may have significantly greater financial, technical and human resource capabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mergers and acquisitions in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries may result in even more resources being concentrated among a smaller number of our competitors.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may also face competition from smaller pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, including specialty pharmaceutical companies and generic drug companies, academic institutions, government agencies and research institutions and others.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The acquisition or licensing of pharmaceutical products is also very competitive, and numerous other companies, including more established companies, have acknowledged strategies to in-license or acquire products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other companies taking similar or different approaches to product acquisitions, including more established companies, may have competitive advantages.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;;font-size: 9pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 36pt 0pt 0pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Our commercial opportunity could be reduced or eliminated if our competitors develop or market products or other novel technologies that are more effective, safer or less costly than any that will be commercialized by us, or obtain regulatory approval for their products more rapidly than we may obtain approval for ours.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our success will be based in part on our ability to identify, develop, and manage a portfolio of drugs that are safer and more effective in the treatment and support of cancer patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Niraparib Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In addition to ZEJULA, there are currently two other commercially available PARP inhibitors.&nbsp;&nbsp;AstraZeneca Plc&#x2019;s LYNPARZA</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">TM</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> (olaparib) was approved in December 2014 by the FDA for use in ovarian cancer patients with a germline BRCA mutation who have been treated with three or more prior lines of chemotherapy, and in August 2017 for the maintenance treatment of adult patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer who are in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy.&nbsp;&nbsp;LYNPARZA was also approved by the EC following a positive opinion by the European Medicines Agency, or EMA, for use as a monotherapy for the maintenance treatment of adult patients with platinum-sensitive relapsed BRCA-mutated (germline and/or somatic) high grade serous epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer who are in complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy.&nbsp;&nbsp;LYNPARZA was also approved in patients with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA-mutated, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative metastatic breast cancer who have previously been treated with chemotherapy in the neoadjuvant, adjuvant or metastatic setting.&nbsp; In February 2018, LYNPARZA received a positive opinion from the EMA&#x2019;s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, or CHMP, for a new tablet formulation and a broad maintenance label, which is expected to lead to an EC marketing authorization in the near future.&nbsp; In July 2017, AstraZeneca and Merck announced a global oncology collaboration to co-develop and co-commercialize LYNPARZA for multiple cancer types.&nbsp;&nbsp;Clovis Oncology, Inc.&#x2019;s RUBRACA</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">TM</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> (rucaparib) was approved in December 2016 by the FDA for use as a monotherapy for the treatment of patients with deleterious BRCA mutation (germline and/or somatic) associated with advanced ovarian cancer who have been treated </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">11</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">with two or more chemotherapies.&nbsp;&nbsp;RUBRACA is currently under FDA review for maintenance treatment following complete or partial response to platinum-based chemotherapy, and is under EMA review as a third-line treatment in advanced ovarian cancer patients with a deleterious BRCA-mutation. &nbsp;In February 2018, the CHMP communicated a positive trend vote (meaning more voted yes than no) for RUBRACA to be authorized for the treatment of a subpopulation of platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer patients who also harbor a BRCA mutation.&nbsp;&nbsp;A final vote will occur at the CHMP&#x2019;s March 2018 meeting.&nbsp; We believe the additional products in clinical development targeting the PARP pathway consist of: Pfizer&#x2019;s talazoparib (MDV3800) and AbbVie&#x2019;s veliparib (ABT-888), both currently in Phase 3 clinical trials; and AbbVie&#x2019;s ABT-767, BeiGene/EMD Serono (Merck KGaA)&#x2019;s pamiparib (BGB-290), Checkpoint Therapeutics&#x2019; CK-102 (formerly CEP-9722) and Hengrui&#x2019;s fluzoparib, each currently in Phase 1 clinical trials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both LYNPARZA and rucaparib have received &#x201C;orphan drug designation&#x201D; from the EMA, which provides certain benefits including market exclusivity for up to ten years in the approved indication post-approval.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In addition to other PARP inhibitors, ZEJULA also competes with AVASTIN</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">TM</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> (bevacizumab), Roche&#x2019;s angiogenesis inhibitor.&nbsp;&nbsp;AVASTIN is FDA- and EMA-approved in combination with chemotherapy for the treatment of recurrent ovarian cancer following platinum-containing chemotherapy (platinum-sensitive and platinum-resistant) and has been approved by the EMA, in combination with chemotherapy, for front-line treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the U.S., it is currently under FDA review for the front-line setting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Rolapitant Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In addition to VARUBI, there are currently three other commercially available branded NK-1 receptor antagonists and two approved generic NK-1 receptor antagonists.&nbsp;&nbsp;Oral aprepitant and its IV pro-drug fosaprepitant, which are both known by the brand name EMEND&#xAE;, are marketed by Merck.&nbsp;&nbsp;IV aprepitant, known by the brand name CINVANTI</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">TM</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">, is marketed by Heron Therapeutics.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe the IV formulation of EMEND accounted for a significant majority of all EMEND usage in the U.S. in 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;A combination of netupitant and palonosetron, known by the brand name AKYNZEO&#xAE;, is marketed by Helsinn Healthcare, or Helsinn, as a combination of NK-1 and 5-HT3 receptor antagonists.&nbsp;&nbsp;Helsinn introduced AKYNZEO in capsule form in October 2014, and has an IV formulation under FDA review.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sandoz launched a generic version of oral aprepitant in late 2016, which competes with oral VARUBI.&nbsp;&nbsp;Glenmark Pharmaceuticals USA also has an FDA-approved generic aprepitant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Immuno-Oncology Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">We are aware of several companies that have antibody-based products on the market or in clinical development that are directed at the same biological targets as some of our immuno-oncology programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are currently two anti-PD-1 antibody products being marketed.&nbsp;&nbsp;OPDIVO&#xAE; (nivolumab), marketed by Bristol-Myers Squibb, is approved in a number of indications as a monotherapy or in combination with other products, including various forms of metastatic melanoma, metastatic NSCLC, advanced renal cell carcinoma, classical Hodgkin lymphoma, or cHL, recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, or HNSCC, locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, microsatellite instability-high, or MSI-H, or mismatch repair deficient, or dMMR, metastatic colorectal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma.&nbsp;&nbsp;KEYTRUDA, marketed by Merck, is approved in a number of indications, including various forms of unresectable or metastatic melanoma, metastatic NSCLC, metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC in the front line setting, recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, refractory cHL, locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, unresectable or metastatic MSI-H or dMMR solid tumors (which includes colorectal cancer), and recurrent locally advanced or metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">There are currently three approved anti-PD-L1 antibodies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Roche&#x2019;s anti-PD-L1 antibody TECENTRIQ&#xAE; (atezolizumab) is approved in patients with various forms of locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma or metastatic NSCLC.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;AstraZeneca&#x2019;s IMFINZI&#xAE; (durvalumab) was approved in 2017 for patients with various forms of locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma.&nbsp;&nbsp;BAVENCIO&#xAE; (avelumab, co-marketed by Merck KGa and Pfizer) was approved in 2017 for adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma and for patients with various forms of locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are aware of several companies that are developing or co-developing anti-PDL-1 and/or anti-PD-1 modulators for various indications, including Novartis, Regeneron/Sanofi, Eli Lilly, Incyte, Boehringer Ingelheim, Celgene/BeiGene, Incyte/Macrogenics, Agenus, CytomX, Symhogen, Checkpoint Therapeutics, and Janssen/Johnson &amp; Johnson.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">There are currently no anti-TIM-3 antibody products or anti-LAG-3 antibody products being marketed.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are aware that two companies, Novartis and Eli Lilly, have anti-TIM-3 modulator antibodies in Phase 1/2 clinical development for </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">12</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">various oncology indications.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are also aware of several companies that have anti-LAG-3 modulators in development for various oncology indications, including Bristol-Myers Squibb, which has an anti-LAG-3 antibody in Phase 2 clinical development; Novartis, which has an anti-LAG-3 antibody in Phase 1/2 and Phase 2 clinical development; and Merck, Boehringer Ingelheim and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, each of which has an anti-LAG-3 antibody in Phase 1 clinical development.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are also aware of several other companies with immuno-oncology antibodies or programs in the preclinical or research phase.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">For more information on the market for cancer therapeutics and oncology supportive care products, our competitors and the products that may compete with our product candidates, see </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">&#x201C;&#x2014;Overview of the Market for Cancer Therapeutics and Oncology Supportive Care Products</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&#x201D;, &#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">&#x2014;Our Product Candidates&#x2014;Niraparib</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&#x201D; and &#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">&#x2014;Our Product Candidates&#x2014; Immuno-Oncology.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Commercial Operations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Our U.S.-based commercial operations team consists of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;">190 </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our European commercial operations team consists of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;background-color: #FFFFFF;">55 </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">employees in nine countries including those at our international headquarters office in Zug, Switzerland.&nbsp;&nbsp;The commercial infrastructure includes a targeted, oncology sales force to establish relationships with a focused group of oncologists, oncology nurses and pharmacists.&nbsp;&nbsp;Personnel in sales management, internal sales training, sales operations, marketing, marketing operations and distribution support the sales force.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the sales, marketing and market access teams manage relationships with key accounts such as managed care organizations, group purchasing organizations, hospital systems, oncology group networks, and government accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;To further develop our commercial infrastructure in the event that any other product candidates receive regulatory approval, we expect to invest significant financial and management resources, much of which will be committed at the risk that any such product candidate may not be approved by any regulatory agency.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9.5pt;">Government Regulation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">As a biopharmaceutical company that operates in the United States, we are subject to extensive regulation by the FDA and other federal, state, and local regulatory agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, or the FDC Act, and the Public Health Service Act, or PHSA, and their implementing regulations set forth, among other things, requirements for the testing, development, manufacture, quality control, safety, effectiveness, approval, labeling, storage, record keeping, reporting, distribution, import, export, advertising and promotion of our products and product candidates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the discussion below focuses on regulation in the United States, we develop and market our products in other countries, including throughout Europe.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, our activities in other countries will be subject to regulation that, although similar in nature and scope in some respects to that imposed in the United States, includes important differences.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, some significant aspects of regulation in the European Union, or the EU, are addressed in a centralized way through the EMA and the EC, but the specific regulation of EU Member States remains essential in many respects for certain types of authorization processes, pricing and reimbursement and promotional activities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Development and Approval</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Under the FDC Act, FDA approval of an NDA is required before any new drug can be marketed in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the PHSA, FDA licensure of a biologics license application, or BLA, is required before a biologic can be marketed in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;NDAs and BLAs require extensive studies and submission of a large amount of data by the applicant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Preclinical Testing.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;Before testing any compound in human subjects in the United States, a company must generate extensive preclinical data.&nbsp;&nbsp;Preclinical testing generally includes laboratory evaluation of product chemistry and formulation, as well as toxicological and pharmacological studies in several animal species to assess the quality and safety of the product.&nbsp;&nbsp;Animal studies must be performed in compliance with the FDA&#x2019;s Good Laboratory Practice, or GLP, regulations and the U.S. Department of Agriculture&#x2019;s Animal Welfare Act.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">IND Application.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;Human clinical trials in the United States cannot commence until an IND application is submitted and becomes effective.&nbsp;&nbsp;A company must submit preclinical testing results to the FDA as part of the IND, and the FDA must evaluate whether there is an adequate basis for testing the drug in initial clinical studies in human volunteers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unless the FDA raises concerns, the IND becomes effective 30&nbsp;days following its receipt by the FDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;Once human clinical trials have commenced, the FDA may stop the clinical trials by placing them on &#x201C;clinical hold&#x201D; because of concerns about the safety of the product being tested, or for other reasons.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">13</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Clinical Trials.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;Clinical trials involve the administration of the drug to healthy human volunteers or to patients, under the supervision of a qualified investigator.&nbsp;&nbsp;The conduct of clinical trials is subject to extensive regulation, including compliance with the FDA&#x2019;s bioresearch monitoring regulations and Good Clinical Practice, or GCP, requirements, which establish standards for conducting, recording data from, and reporting the results of, clinical trials, and are intended to assure that the data and reported results are credible and accurate, and that the rights, safety, and well-being of study participants are protected.&nbsp;&nbsp;Clinical trials must be conducted under protocols that detail the study objectives, parameters for monitoring safety, and the efficacy criteria, if any, to be evaluated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each protocol is reviewed by the FDA as part of the IND.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, each clinical trial must be reviewed and approved by, and conducted under the auspices of, an institutional review board, or IRB.&nbsp;&nbsp;Companies sponsoring the clinical trials, investigators, and IRBs also must comply with applicable regulations and guidelines for obtaining informed consent from the study subjects, following the protocol and investigational plan, adequately monitoring the clinical trial, and timely reporting of adverse events.&nbsp;&nbsp;Foreign studies conducted under an IND must meet the same requirements that apply to studies being conducted in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;Data from a foreign study not conducted under an IND may be submitted in support of an NDA or BLA if the study was conducted in accordance with GCP and the FDA is able to validate the data.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">A study sponsor is required to publicly post certain details about active clinical trials and clinical trial results on government or independent websites (e.g.,&nbsp;http://clinicaltrials.gov).&nbsp;&nbsp;Human clinical trials typically are conducted in three sequential phases, although the phases may overlap with one another:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:9pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Phase&nbsp;1 clinical trials include the initial administration of the investigational drug to humans, typically to a small group of healthy human subjects, but occasionally to a group of patients with the targeted disease or disorder.&nbsp;&nbsp;Phase&nbsp;1 clinical trials generally are intended to determine the metabolism and pharmacologic actions of the drug, the side effects associated with increasing doses, and, if possible, to gain early evidence of effectiveness.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:9pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Phase&nbsp;2 clinical trials generally are controlled studies that involve a relatively small sample of the intended patient population, and are designed to develop data regarding the product&#x2019;s effectiveness, to determine dose response and the optimal dose range, and to gather additional information relating to safety and potential adverse effects.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:36pt;"><p style="width:36pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:9pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Phase&nbsp;3 clinical trials are conducted after preliminary evidence of effectiveness has been obtained, and are intended to gather the additional information about safety and effectiveness necessary to evaluate the drug&#x2019;s overall risk-benefit profile, and to provide a basis for physician labeling.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, Phase&nbsp;3 clinical development programs consist of expanded, large-scale studies of patients with the target disease or disorder to obtain statistical evidence of the efficacy and safety of the drug at the proposed dosing regimen, or the safety, purity, and potency of a biological product.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The sponsoring company, the FDA, or the IRB may suspend or terminate a clinical trial at any time on various grounds, including a finding that the subjects are being exposed to an unacceptable health risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, success in early-stage clinical trials does not assure success in later-stage clinical trials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Data obtained from clinical activities are not always conclusive and may be subject to alternative interpretations that could delay, limit or prevent regulatory approval.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">NDA/BLA Submission and Review.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;After completing clinical testing of an investigational drug or biologic, a sponsor must prepare and submit an NDA or BLA for review and approval by the FDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The NDA is a comprehensive, multi-volume application that includes, among other things, the results of preclinical and clinical studies, information about the drug&#x2019;s composition, and the sponsor&#x2019;s plans for manufacturing, packaging, and labeling the drug.&nbsp; For certain candidates, such as immunotherapeutic antibodies, this information is submitted in a BLA.&nbsp; When an NDA or BLA is submitted, the FDA conducts a preliminary review to determine whether the application is sufficiently complete to be accepted for filing.&nbsp;&nbsp;If it is not, the FDA may refuse to file the application and request additional information, in which case the application must be resubmitted with the supplemental information, and review of the application is delayed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">FDA performance goals generally provide for action on an application within 12 months of submission, but that deadline is extended in certain circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, the review process is often significantly extended by FDA requests for additional information or clarification.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA also has programs intended to expedite the development and review of new drugs intended to address unmet medical needs for serious or life-threatening conditions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Through priority review designation, for example, the FDA can expedite the target action date to eight&nbsp;months from application submission, if the agency finds that a drug is intended to treat a serious condition and, if approved, would provide a significant improvement in </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">14</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>
