</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">safety or effectiveness.&nbsp;&nbsp;Another example is fast-track designation, which the FDA may grant to a drug that is intended to treat a serious condition and that demonstrates the potential to address an unmet medical need.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the fast track program, the FDA allows a sponsor to submit completed portions of an NDA on a rolling basis, rather than requiring the entire application to be submitted before review begins.&nbsp;&nbsp;Product candidates with fast-track designation also may be eligible for more frequent meetings or correspondence with the agency during the development process.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">As part of its review, the FDA may refer an NDA or BLA to an advisory committee for evaluation and a recommendation as to whether the application should be approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the FDA is not bound by the recommendation of an advisory committee, the agency usually has followed such recommendations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA may determine that a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy, or REMS, is necessary to ensure that the benefits of a new product outweigh its risks, and the product can therefore be approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;A REMS may include various elements, ranging from a medication guide or&nbsp;patient package insert to limitations on who may prescribe or dispense the drug, depending on what the FDA considers necessary for the safe use of the drug.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the Pediatric Research Equity Act, certain applications for approval must include an assessment, generally based on clinical study data, of the safety and effectiveness of the subject drug or biological product in relevant pediatric populations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">After review of an NDA or BLA, the FDA may decide to not approve the application or issue a complete response letter outlining the deficiencies in the submission.&nbsp; The complete response letter also may request additional information, including additional preclinical or clinical data.&nbsp;&nbsp;Even if such additional information and data are submitted, the FDA may decide that the NDA still does not meet the standards for approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;Data from clinical trials are not always conclusive and the FDA may interpret data differently than the sponsor.&nbsp;&nbsp;Obtaining regulatory approval often takes a number of years, involves the expenditure of substantial resources, and depends on a number of factors, including the severity of the disease in question, the availability of alternative treatments, and the risks and benefits demonstrated in clinical trials.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, as a condition of approval, the FDA may impose restrictions that could affect the commercial success of a drug or require post-approval commitments, including the completion within a specified time period of additional clinical studies, which often are referred to as &#x201C;Phase&nbsp;4&#x201D; or &#x201C;post-marketing&#x201D; studies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Post-approval modifications to the drug or biologic product, such as changes in indications, labeling, or manufacturing processes or facilities, may require a sponsor to develop additional data or conduct additional preclinical or clinical trials, to be submitted in a new or supplemental NDA or BLA, which would require FDA approval.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Post-Approval Regulation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Once approved, products are subject to continuing regulation by the FDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;If ongoing regulatory requirements are not met or if safety problems occur after the product reaches the market, the FDA may at any time withdraw product approval or take actions that would limit or suspend marketing.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the FDA may require post-marketing studies or clinical trials if new safety information develops.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Good Manufacturing Practices.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;Companies engaged in manufacturing drug products or their components must comply with applicable current Good Manufacturing Practice, or cGMP, requirements and product-specific regulations enforced by the FDA and other regulatory agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Compliance with cGMP includes adhering to requirements relating to organization and training of personnel, buildings and facilities, equipment, control of components and drug product containers and closures, production and process controls, quality control and quality assurance, packaging and labeling controls, holding and distribution, laboratory controls, and records and reports.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA regulates and inspects equipment, facilities, and processes used in manufacturing pharmaceutical or biologic products, prior to approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;If, after receiving approval, a company makes a material change in manufacturing equipment, location, or process (all of which are, to some degree, incorporated in the NDA or BLA), additional regulatory review and approval may be required.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA also conducts regular, periodic visits to re-inspect equipment, facilities, and processes following the initial approval of a product.&nbsp;&nbsp;Failure to comply with applicable cGMP requirements and conditions of product approval may lead the FDA to seek sanctions, including fines, civil penalties, injunctions, suspension of manufacturing operations, operating restrictions, withdrawal of FDA approval, seizure or recall of products, and criminal prosecution.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although we periodically monitor the FDA compliance of our third-party manufacturers, we cannot be certain that our present or future third-party manufacturers will consistently comply with cGMP and other applicable FDA regulatory requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Advertising and Promotion.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;The FDA and other federal regulatory agencies closely regulate the marketing and promotion of drugs and biologics through, among other things, standards and regulations for direct-to-consumer advertising, advertising and promotion to healthcare professionals, communications regarding unapproved uses, industry-sponsored </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">15</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">scientific and educational activities, and promotional activities involving the Internet.&nbsp;&nbsp;A product cannot be commercially promoted before it is approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;After approval, product promotion can include only those claims relating to safety and effectiveness that are consistent with the labeling approved by the FDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;Healthcare providers are permitted to prescribe drugs and biologics for &#x201C;off-label&#x201D; uses&#x2014;that is, uses not approved by the FDA and therefore not described in the product&#x2019;s labeling&#x2014;because the FDA does not regulate the practice of medicine.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, FDA regulations impose stringent restrictions on manufacturers&#x2019; communications regarding off-label uses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Broadly speaking, a manufacturer may not promote a drug or biologic for off-label use, but under certain conditions may engage in non-promotional, balanced, scientific communication regarding off-label use.&nbsp;&nbsp;Failure to comply with applicable FDA requirements and restrictions in this area may subject a company to adverse publicity and enforcement action by the FDA, the Department of Justice, or the Office of Inspector General of the Department of Health and Human Services, as well as state authorities.&nbsp;&nbsp;This could subject a company to a range of penalties that could have a significant commercial impact, including civil and criminal fines and agreements that materially restrict the manner in which a company promotes or distributes drug or biological products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Other Requirements.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;In addition, companies that manufacture or distribute drug or biological products or that hold approved NDAs or BLAs must comply with other regulatory requirements, including submitting annual reports, reporting information about adverse drug experiences, and maintaining certain records.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Hatch-Waxman Act</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act of 1984, or the Hatch-Waxman Act, establishes two abbreviated approval pathways for pharmaceutical products that are in some way follow-on versions of already approved products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Generic Drugs.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;A generic version of an approved drug is approved by means of an abbreviated new drug application, or ANDA, by which the sponsor demonstrates that the proposed product is the same as the approved, brand-name drug, which is referred to as the &#x201C;reference listed drug,&#x201D; or RLD.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, an ANDA must contain data and information showing that the proposed generic product and RLD (1)&nbsp;have the same active ingredient, in the same strength and dosage form, to be delivered via the same route of administration, (2)&nbsp;are intended for the same uses, and (3)&nbsp;are bioequivalent.&nbsp;&nbsp;This is instead of independently demonstrating the proposed product&#x2019;s safety and effectiveness, which are inferred from the fact that the product is the same as the RLD, which the FDA previously found to be safe and effective.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">505(b)(2)&nbsp;NDAs.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;If a product is similar, but not identical, to an already approved product, it may be submitted for approval via an NDA under Section&nbsp;505(b)(2) of the FDC Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unlike an ANDA, this does not excuse the sponsor from demonstrating the proposed product&#x2019;s safety and effectiveness.&nbsp;&nbsp;Rather, the sponsor is permitted to rely to some degree on the FDA&#x2019;s finding that the RLD is safe and effective, and must submit its own product-specific data of safety and effectiveness to an extent necessary because of the differences between the products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">RLD Patents.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;An NDA sponsor must identify to the FDA patents that claim the drug substance or drug product or a method of using the drug.&nbsp;&nbsp;When the drug is approved, those patents are among the information about the product that is listed in the FDA publication, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">, which is referred to as the </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Orange Book</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;The sponsor of an ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application seeking to rely on an approved product as the RLD must make one of several certifications regarding each listed patent.&nbsp;&nbsp;A &#x201C;Paragraph&nbsp;III&#x201D; certification is the sponsor&#x2019;s statement that it will wait for the patent to expire before obtaining approval for its product.&nbsp;&nbsp;A &#x201C;Paragraph&nbsp;IV&#x201D; certification is an assertion that the patent does not block approval of the later product, either because the patent is invalid or unenforceable or because the patent, even if valid, is not infringed by the new product.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Regulatory Exclusivities.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;The Hatch-Waxman Act provides periods of regulatory exclusivity for products that would serve as RLDs for an ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application.&nbsp;&nbsp;If a product is a &#x201C;new chemical entity,&#x201D; or NCE&#x2014;generally meaning that the active moiety has never before been approved in any drug&#x2014;there is a period of five years from the product&#x2019;s approval during which the FDA may not accept for filing any ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application for a drug with the same active moiety.&nbsp;&nbsp;An ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application may be submitted after four years, however, if its sponsor makes a Paragraph&nbsp;IV certification.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">A product that is not an NCE may qualify for a three-year period of exclusivity if the NDA contains new clinical data, derived from studies conducted by or for the sponsor, that were necessary for approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;In that instance, the exclusivity period does not preclude filing or review of the ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application; rather, the FDA is precluded from granting final approval to the ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application until three years after approval of the RLD.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the exclusivity </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">16</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">applies only to the conditions of approval that required submission of the clinical data.&nbsp; For example, if an NDA is submitted for a product that is not an NCE, but that seeks approval for a new indication, and clinical data were required to demonstrate the safety or effectiveness of the product for that use, the FDA will not finally approve an ANDA or 505(b)(2) application for another product with that active moiety for that use until the expiration of the applicable three-year period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Once the FDA accepts for filing an ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application containing a Paragraph&nbsp;IV certification, the applicant must within 20&nbsp;days provide notice to the RLD NDA holder and patent owner that the application has been submitted, and provide the factual and legal basis for the applicant&#x2019;s assertion that the patent is invalid or not infringed.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the NDA holder or patent owner files suit against the ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;applicant for patent infringement within 45&nbsp;days of receiving the Paragraph&nbsp;IV notice, the FDA is prohibited from approving the ANDA or 505(b)(2)&nbsp;application for a period of 30&nbsp;months or the resolution of the underlying suit, whichever is earlier.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the RLD has NCE exclusivity and the notice is given and suit filed during the fifth year of exclusivity, the 30-month stay does not begin until five years after the RLD approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA may approve the proposed product before the expiration of the 30-month stay if a court finds the patent invalid or not infringed or if the court shortens the period because the parties have failed to cooperate in expediting the litigation.&nbsp;&nbsp;At present, each of rolapitant and niraparib is an NCE with five-year NCE exclusivity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Patent Term Restoration.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;A portion of the patent term lost during product development and FDA review of an NDA or BLA is restored if approval of the application is the first permitted commercial marketing of a drug containing the active ingredient.&nbsp;&nbsp;The patent term restoration period is generally one-half the time between the effective date of the IND or the date of patent grant (whichever is later) and the date of submission of the NDA or BLA, plus the time between the date of submission of the NDA or BLA and the date of FDA approval of the product.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum period of restoration is five years, and the patent cannot be extended to more than 14&nbsp;years from the date of FDA approval of the product.&nbsp;&nbsp;Only one patent claiming each approved product is eligible for restoration and the patent holder must apply for restoration within 60&nbsp;days of approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;The U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, or the USPTO, in consultation with the FDA, reviews and approves the application for patent term restoration.&nbsp;&nbsp;When any of our products is approved, we intend to seek patent term restoration for an applicable patent when it is appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;At present, we anticipate that rolapitant and niraparib will qualify for patent term restoration.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have applied for patent term restoration for rolapitant and niraparib.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">The Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act, or BPCI Act, authorizes the FDA to license a biological product that is biosimilar to an FDA-licensed biologic through an abbreviated pathway.&nbsp;&nbsp;The BPCI Act establishes criteria for determining that a product is biosimilar to an already-licensed biologic, or reference product, and establishes a process by which an abbreviated BLA for a biosimilar product is submitted, reviewed and approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;The BPCI Act provides periods of exclusivity that protect a reference product from biosimilars competition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the BPCI Act, the FDA may not accept a biosimilar application for review until four years after the date of first licensure of the reference product, and the biosimilar may not be licensed until at least 12 years after the reference product&#x2019;s approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the BPCI Act establishes procedures by which the biosimilar applicant provides information about its application and product to the reference product sponsor, and by which information about potentially relevant patents may be shared and litigation over patents may proceed in advance of approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;The BPCI Act also provides a period of exclusivity for the first biosimilar determined by the FDA to be interchangeable with the reference product.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">We anticipate that the contours of the BPCI Act will continue to be defined as the statute is implemented over a period of years.&nbsp;&nbsp;This likely will be accomplished by a variety of means, including decisions related to the statute by the relevant federal courts, FDA issuance of guidance documents, and FDA decisions in the course of considering specific applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;The FDA has to date issued various guidance documents and other materials indicating the agency&#x2019;s thinking regarding a number of issues implicated by the BPCI Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the FDA&#x2019;s approval of several biosimilar applications in recent years has helped define the agency&#x2019;s approach to certain issues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">17</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">America Invents Act</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">As part of the passage of the America Invents Act in 2011, new post-grant review proceedings were added to U.S. patent law.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among these procedures are post-grant reviews and inter partes reviews, which allow any member of the public to file a petition with the USPTO seeking to review the patentability of one or more claims in an issued U.S. patent.&nbsp;&nbsp;Post-grant review proceedings are conducted before Administrative Patent Judges in the USPTO using a lower standard of proof than used in Federal District Court.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the challenged patents are not accorded a presumption of validity as they are in Federal District Court.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Other Exclusivities</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Pediatric Exclusivity.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;Section&nbsp;505A of the FDC Act provides for six months of additional exclusivity and patent protection if an NDA sponsor submits pediatric data that fairly respond to a written request from the FDA for such data.&nbsp;&nbsp;The data does not need to show the product to be effective in the pediatric population studied; rather, if the clinical trial is deemed to fairly respond to the FDA&#x2019;s request, the additional protection is granted.&nbsp;&nbsp;If reports of requested pediatric studies are submitted to and accepted by the FDA within the statutory time limits, whatever statutory or regulatory periods of exclusivity or </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Orange Book</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> listed patent protection that cover the drug are extended by six months.&nbsp; This is not a patent term extension, but it effectively extends the regulatory period during which the FDA cannot approve an ANDA or 505(b)(2) application with reference to RLD owing to regulatory exclusivity or listed patents.&nbsp;&nbsp;The BPCI Act incorporates by reference many provisions of Section 505A of the FDC Act, such that if pediatric studies for a biological product fairly respond to a written request from the FDA, are completed in a timely fashion, and otherwise comply with applicable requirements, the 12-year exclusivity period will be deemed to be 12 and a half years, and the four year period will be deemed to be four and a half years.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, six-month pediatric exclusivity does not attach to patents for a biological product under the BPCI Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;When any of our products is approved, we anticipate seeking pediatric exclusivity when it is appropriate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Orphan Drug Exclusivity.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> &nbsp;The Orphan Drug Act provides incentives for the development of drugs and biological products intended to treat rare diseases or conditions, which generally are diseases or conditions affecting less than 200,000 individuals in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;If a sponsor demonstrates that a drug or biologic is intended to treat a rare disease or condition, the FDA grants orphan drug designation to the product for that use.&nbsp;&nbsp;The benefits of orphan drug designation include research and development tax credits and exemption from user fees.&nbsp;&nbsp;A drug or biologic that is approved for the orphan drug designated indication is granted seven years of orphan drug exclusivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;During that period, the FDA generally may not approve any other application for the same product for the same indication, although there are exceptions, most notably when the later product is shown to be clinically superior to the product with exclusivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;We intend to seek orphan drug designation and exclusivity for our products whenever it is available.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">21st Century Cures Act</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In December 2016, the United States Congress passed the 21</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;font-size:5pt;top:-4pt;position:relative;line-height:100%">st</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;"> Century Cures Act, or the Cures Act, which includes a number of provisions designed to speed development of innovative therapies, provide funding authorization to the National Institutes of Health, or NIH, and provide funding for certain oncology-directed research.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because the Cures Act was enacted recently, it is difficult to know whether or how it will directly affect our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, it also includes a provision which requires us to post our policies on the availability of certain expanded access programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Cures Act includes provisions that may be beneficial to us in the future, including a requirement that the FDA assess and publish guidance on the use of novel clinical trial designs, the use of real world evidence in applications, the availability of summary level review for supplemental applications for certain indications, and the qualification of drug development tools.&nbsp;&nbsp;Because these provisions allow the FDA several years to develop these policies, their effects on us, if any, could be delayed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The Cures Act also authorizes $1.8 billion in funding for the &#x201C;Cancer Moonshot&#x201D; initiative.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Cancer Moonshot initiative&#x2019;s strategic goals encourage inter-agency cooperation and fund research and innovation to catalyze new scientific breakthroughs, bring new therapies to patients, and strengthen prevention and diagnosis.&nbsp;&nbsp;This initiative aims to stimulate drug development through the creation of a public-private partnership with 20 to 30 pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to expedite cancer researchers&#x2019; access to investigational agents and approved drugs.&nbsp;&nbsp;This partnership is designed to permit researchers to obtain drugs and other technologies from a preapproved &#x201C;formulary&#x201D; list without having to negotiate with each company for individual research projects.&nbsp;&nbsp;We will continue to monitor these developments to assess their potential impacts on our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">18</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Foreign Regulation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In addition to laws and regulations in the United States, we are subject to a variety of laws and regulations in other jurisdictions governing, among other things, clinical trials and any commercial sales and distribution of our products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Whether or not we obtain FDA approval for a product, we must obtain the requisite marketing authorizations from regulatory authorities in foreign countries prior to the commencement of clinical trials or marketing of a product in those countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain countries outside of the United States have a similar process that requires the submission of a clinical trial application, or CTA, much like an IND, prior to the commencement of clinical trials.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the EU, for example, a CTA must be submitted to the national health authority of each EU Member State in which the clinical trial is to be conducted and to an independent ethics committee, much like the FDA and an IRB, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Once the CTA is approved in accordance with a country&#x2019;s requirements, clinical trial development may proceed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The requirements and process governing the conduct of clinical trials, product licensing, pricing and reimbursement vary from country to country.&nbsp;&nbsp;In all cases in EU Member States, for example, the clinical trials must be conducted in accordance with GCP, applicable regulatory requirements, and ethical principles that have their origin in the Declaration of Helsinki.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In the EU, a marketing authorization for a medicinal product can be obtained through a centralized, mutual recognition, decentralized procedure, or national procedure (single EU Member State).&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with the centralized procedure, the applicant can submit a single application for marketing authorization to the EMA that will provide a positive opinion regarding the application if it meets certain quality, safety, and efficacy requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Following the opinion of the EMA, the EC makes a final decision to grant a centralized marketing authorization that permits the marketing of a product in all 28 EU Member States and three of the four European Free Trade Association, or EFTA, States,&nbsp;Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway.&nbsp;&nbsp;The centralized procedure is mandatory for certain medicinal products, including orphan medicinal products, medicinal products derived from certain biotechnological processes, advanced therapy medicinal products and certain other medicinal products containing a new active substance for the treatment of certain diseases, and optional for certain other products, including medicinal products that are a significant therapeutic, scientific or technical innovation, or whose authorization would be in the interest of public or animal health.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the centralized procedure in the EU, the maximum timeframe for the evaluation of a marketing authorization application is 210 days (excluding clock stops, when additional written or oral information is to be provided by the applicant in response to questions asked by the CHMP).&nbsp;&nbsp;Accelerated evaluation may be granted by the CHMP in exceptional cases.&nbsp;&nbsp;These are defined as circumstances in which a medicinal product is expected to be of a &#x201C;major public health interest&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;Three cumulative criteria must be fulfilled in such circumstances: the seriousness of the disease, such as heavy disabling or life-threatening diseases, to be treated; the absence or insufficiency of an appropriate alternative therapeutic approach; and anticipation of high therapeutic benefit.&nbsp;&nbsp;In these circumstances, the EMA ensures that the opinion of the CHMP is given within 150 days.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Unlike the centralized authorization procedure, the decentralized marketing authorization procedure requires a separate application to, and leads to separate approval by, the competent authorities of each EU Member State in which the product is to be marketed.&nbsp;&nbsp;This application is identical to the application that would be submitted to the EMA for authorization through the centralized procedure.&nbsp;&nbsp;The reference EU Member State prepares a draft assessment and drafts of the related materials within 120 days after receipt of a valid application.&nbsp;&nbsp;The resulting assessment report is submitted to the concerned EU Member States who, within 90 days of receipt, must decide whether to approve the assessment report and related materials.&nbsp;&nbsp;If a concerned EU Member State cannot approve the assessment report and related materials due to concerns relating to a potential serious risk to public health, disputed elements may be referred to the EC, whose decision is binding on all EU Member States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The mutual recognition procedure similarly is based on the acceptance by the competent authorities of the EU Member States of the marketing authorization of a medicinal product by the competent authorities of other EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The holder of a national marketing authorization may submit an application to the competent authority of an EU Member State requesting that this authority recognize the marketing authorization delivered by the competent authority of another EU Member State.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">A medicinal product may be granted an orphan designation in the EU if: (i) it would be used to treat or prevent a life-threatening or chronically debilitating condition and either affects no more than five in 10,000 people in the EU or for economic reasons would be unlikely to be developed without incentives; and (ii) no satisfactory method of diagnosis, prevention or treatment of the condition concerned exists, or, if such a method exists, the medicinal product would be of </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">19</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">significant benefit to those affected by the condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;The application for orphan designation must be submitted to the EMA and approved prior to market authorization.&nbsp;&nbsp;Once authorized, orphan medicinal products are entitled to ten years of market exclusivity.&nbsp;&nbsp;During this ten-year period, with limited exceptions, neither the competent authorities of the EU Member States, the EMA, nor the EC are permitted to accept applications or grant marketing authorization for other similar medicinal products with the same therapeutic indication.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, marketing authorization may be granted to a similar medicinal product with the same orphan indication during that period with the consent of the holder of the marketing authorization or if the manufacturer of the product is unable to supply sufficient quantities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Marketing authorization may also be granted to a similar medicinal product with the same orphan indication if the latter product is safer, more effective or otherwise clinically superior to the original product.&nbsp;&nbsp;The period of market exclusivity may be reduced to six years if it can be demonstrated on the basis of available evidence that the original orphan medicinal product is sufficiently profitable not to justify maintenance of market exclusivity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Once an applicant receives marketing authorization in an EU Member State, through any application route, the applicant is then required to engage in pricing discussions and negotiations with a separate pricing authority in that country.&nbsp;&nbsp;The legislators, policymakers and healthcare insurance funds in the EU Member States continue to propose and implement cost-containing measures to keep healthcare costs down, due in part to the attention being paid to health care cost containment and other austerity measures in the EU.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain of these changes could impose limitations on the prices pharmaceutical companies are able to charge for their products.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amounts of reimbursement available from governmental agencies or third-party payors for these products may increase the tax obligations on pharmaceutical companies such as ours, or may facilitate the introduction of generic competition with respect to our products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Furthermore, an increasing number of EU Member States and other foreign countries use prices for medicinal products established in other countries as &#x201C;reference prices&#x201D; to help determine the price of the product in their own territory.&nbsp;&nbsp;Consequently, a downward trend in prices of medicinal products in some countries could contribute to similar downward trends elsewhere.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the ongoing budgetary difficulties faced by a number of EU Member States, including Greece and Spain, have led and may continue to lead to substantial delays in payment and payment partially with government bonds rather than cash for medicinal products, which could negatively impact our revenues and profitability.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, in order to obtain reimbursement of our medicinal products in some countries, including some EU Member States, we may be required to conduct clinical trials that compare the cost-effectiveness of our products to other available therapies.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that our medicinal products will obtain favorable reimbursement status in any country.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The sole legal instrument at the EU level governing the pricing and reimbursement of medicinal products is Council Directive 89/105/EEC, or the Transparency Directive.&nbsp;&nbsp;The aim of this directive is to ensure that pricing and reimbursement mechanisms established in the EU Member States are transparent and objective, do not hinder the free movement and trade of medicinal products in the EU and do not hinder, prevent or distort competition on the market.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Transparency Directive does not provide any guidance concerning the specific criteria on the basis of which pricing and reimbursement decisions are to be made in individual EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;Neither does it have any direct consequence for pricing nor reimbursement levels in individual EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The EU Member States are free to restrict the range of medicinal products for which their national health insurance systems provide reimbursement and to control the prices and/or reimbursement levels of medicinal products for human use.&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain individual EU Member States adopt policies according to which a specific price or level of reimbursement is approved for the medicinal product.&nbsp;&nbsp;Others adopt a system of reference pricing, basing the price or reimbursement level in their territories either on the pricing and reimbursement levels in other countries or on the pricing and reimbursement levels of medicinal products intended for the same therapeutic indication.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, some EU Member States impose direct or indirect controls on the profitability of the company placing the medicinal product on the market.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Health Technology Assessment, or HTA, of medicinal products is becoming an increasingly common part of the pricing and reimbursement procedures in some EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;These EU Member States include the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy and Sweden.&nbsp;&nbsp;The HTA process in European Economic Area, or EEA, countries is governed by the national laws of these countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;HTA is the procedure according to which the assessment of the public health impact, therapeutic impact and the economic and societal impact of use of a given medicinal product in the national healthcare systems of the individual country is conducted.&nbsp;&nbsp;HTA generally focuses on the clinical efficacy and effectiveness, safety, cost, and cost-effectiveness of individual medicinal products as well as their potential implications for the healthcare system.&nbsp;&nbsp;Those elements of medicinal products are compared with other treatment options available on the market.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The outcome of HTA regarding specific medicinal products will often influence the pricing and reimbursement status granted to these medicinal products by the competent authorities of individual EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The extent to which pricing and reimbursement decisions are influenced by the HTA of the specific medicinal product vary between EU Member States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">20</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In 2011, Directive 2011/24/EU was adopted at the EU level.&nbsp;&nbsp;This directive concerns the application of patients&#x2019; rights in cross-border healthcare.&nbsp;&nbsp;This directive is intended to establish rules&nbsp;for facilitating access to safe and high-quality cross-border healthcare in the EU.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to this directive, a voluntary network of national authorities or bodies responsible for HTA in the individual EU Member States was established.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purpose of the network is to facilitate and support the exchange of scientific information concerning HTAs.&nbsp;&nbsp;This may lead to harmonization of the criteria taken into account in the conduct of HTAs between EU Member States and in pricing and reimbursement decisions and may negatively affect price in at least some EU Member States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In the EU, the advertising and promotion of our products will also be subject to EU Member States&#x2019; laws concerning promotion of medicinal products, interactions with physicians, misleading and comparative advertising and unfair commercial practices, as well as other EU Member State legislation that may apply to the advertising and promotion of medicinal products.&nbsp;&nbsp;These laws require that promotional materials and advertising in relation to medicinal products comply with the product&#x2019;s Summary of Product Characteristics, or SmPC, as approved by the competent authorities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The SmPC is the document that provides information to physicians concerning the safe and effective use of the medicinal product.&nbsp;&nbsp;It forms an intrinsic and integral part of the marketing authorization granted for the medicinal product.&nbsp;&nbsp;Promotion of a medicinal product that does not comply with the SmPC is considered to constitute off-label promotion.&nbsp;&nbsp;The off-label promotion of medicinal products is prohibited in the EU.&nbsp;&nbsp;The applicable laws at the EU level and in the individual EU Member States also prohibit the direct-to-consumer advertising of prescription-only medicinal products.&nbsp;&nbsp;Violations of the rules&nbsp;governing the promotion of medicinal products in the EU could be penalized by administrative measures, fines and imprisonment.&nbsp;&nbsp;These laws may further limit or restrict communications concerning the advertising and promotion of our products to the general public and may also impose limitations on our promotional activities with healthcare professionals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Failure to comply with the EU Member State laws implementing the Community Code on medicinal products, and EU rules&nbsp;governing the promotion of medicinal products, interactions with physicians, misleading and comparative advertising and unfair commercial practices, with the EU Member State laws that apply to the promotion of medicinal products, statutory health insurance, bribery and anti-corruption or with other applicable regulatory requirements can result in enforcement action by the EU Member State authorities, which may include any of the following: fines, imprisonment, orders forfeiting products or prohibiting or suspending their supply to the market, or requiring the manufacturer to issue public warnings, or to conduct a product recall.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Interactions between pharmaceutical companies and physicians are also governed by strict laws, regulations, industry self-regulation codes of conduct and physicians&#x2019; codes of professional conduct in the individual EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;The provision of benefits or advantages to physicians to induce or encourage the prescription, recommendation, endorsement, purchase, supply, order or use of medicinal products is prohibited in the EU.&nbsp;&nbsp;The provision of benefits or advantages to physicians is also governed by the national anti-bribery laws of the EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;One example is the UK Bribery Act of 2010, or the UK Bribery Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;This act applies to any company incorporated in or &#x201C;carrying on business&#x201D; in the UK, irrespective of where in the world the alleged bribery activity occurs.&nbsp;&nbsp;This act could have implications for our interactions with physicians in and outside the UK.&nbsp;&nbsp;Violation of these laws could result in substantial fines and imprisonment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The national laws of certain EU Member States require payments made to physicians to be publicly disclosed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Moreover, the European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries and Associations, or EFPIA, Code on disclosure of transfers of value from pharmaceutical companies to healthcare professionals and healthcare organizations imposes a general obligation on members of the EFPIA or related national industry bodies to disclose transfers of value to healthcare professionals.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, agreements with physicians must often be the subject of prior notification and approval by the physician&#x2019;s employer, his/her competent professional organization, and/or the competent authorities of the individual EU Member States.&nbsp;&nbsp;These requirements are provided in the national laws, industry codes, or professional codes of conduct, applicable in the EU Member States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">For other countries outside of the EU, such as countries in Eastern Europe, Central and South America or Asia, the requirements governing the conduct of clinical trials, product licensing, pricing and reimbursement vary from country to country.&nbsp;&nbsp;In all cases, again, the clinical trials are conducted in accordance with GCP, applicable regulatory requirements, and ethical principles that have their origin in the Declaration of Helsinki.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">If we fail to comply with applicable foreign regulatory requirements, we may be subject to, among other things, warning letters or untitled letters, injunctions, civil, administrative, or criminal penalties, monetary fines or imprisonment, suspension or withdrawal of regulatory approvals, suspension of ongoing clinical studies, refusal to approve pending </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">21</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">applications or supplements to applications filed by us, suspension or the imposition of restrictions on operations, product recalls, the refusal to permit the import or export of our products or the seizure or detention of products.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:9.5pt;">Coverage and Reimbursement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Significant uncertainty exists as to the coverage and reimbursement status of any products for which we have or may obtain regulatory approval.&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales of ZEJULA, VARUBI, and any of our other product candidates will depend, in part, on the extent to which the costs of the products will be covered by third-party payors, including government healthcare programs such as Medicare and Medicaid, commercial health insurers and managed care organizations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The process for determining whether a payor will provide coverage for a product may be separate from the process for setting the price or reimbursement rate that the payor will pay for the product once coverage is approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;Third-party payors may limit coverage to specific products on an approved list, or formulary, which might not include all FDA-approved products for a particular indication.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In order to secure coverage and reimbursement for ZEJULA, VARUBI, or any other product that might be approved for sale, we may need to conduct expensive pharmacoeconomic studies in order to demonstrate the medical necessity and cost-effectiveness of the product, in addition to the costs required to obtain FDA or other comparable regulatory approvals.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our product candidates may not be considered medically necessary or cost-effective.&nbsp;&nbsp;A payor&#x2019;s decision to provide coverage for a product does not imply that an adequate reimbursement rate will be approved.&nbsp;&nbsp;Third-party reimbursement may not be sufficient to enable us to maintain price levels high enough to realize an appropriate return on our investment in product development.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In the past, payors have implemented reimbursement metrics and periodically revised those metrics as well as the methodologies used as the basis for reimbursement rates, such as average sales price, or ASP, average manufacturer price, or AMP, and actual acquisition cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;The existing data for reimbursement based on these metrics is relatively limited, although certain states have begun to survey acquisition cost data for the purpose of setting Medicaid reimbursement rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, or CMS, surveys and publishes retail pharmacy acquisition cost information in the form of National Average Drug Acquisition Cost, or NADAC, files to provide state Medicaid agencies with a basis of comparison for their own reimbursement and pricing methodologies and rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;It may be difficult to project the impact of these evolving reimbursement mechanics on the willingness of payors to cover our products for which we receive regulatory approval.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Our participation in the Medicaid rebate program established by the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1990 and under multiple subsequent amendments of that law, including the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, as amended by the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of 2010, together the ACA, requires us to pay a rebate for each unit of drug reimbursed by Medicaid.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amount of the &#x201C;basic&#x201D; portion of the rebate for each product is set by law as the larger of: (i) 23.1% of quarterly AMP, or (ii) the difference between quarterly AMP and the quarterly best price available from us to any commercial or non-governmental customer, or Best Price.&nbsp;&nbsp;AMP must be reported on a monthly and quarterly basis and Best Price is reported on a quarterly basis only.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the rebate also includes the &#x201C;additional&#x201D; portion, which adjusts the overall rebate amount upward as an &#x201C;inflation penalty&#x201D; when the drug&#x2019;s latest quarter&#x2019;s AMP exceeds the drug&#x2019;s AMP from the first full quarter of sales after launch, adjusted for increases in the Consumer Price Index&#x2014;Urban.&nbsp;&nbsp;The upward adjustment in the rebate amount per unit is equal to the excess amount of the current AMP over the inflation-adjusted AMP from the first full quarter of sales.&nbsp;&nbsp;The rebate amount is required to be recomputed each quarter based on our report to CMS of current quarterly AMP and Best Price for our drug.&nbsp;&nbsp;The terms of our participation in the program impose a requirement for us to report revisions to AMP or Best Price within a period not to exceed 12 quarters from the quarter in which the data was originally due.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any such revisions could have the impact of increasing or decreasing our rebate liability for prior quarters, depending on the direction of the revision.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ACA and subsequent legislation also changed the definition of AMP.&nbsp;&nbsp;In February 2016, final guidance and regulations were issued by the federal government clarifying these and certain other ACA changes and which relate to the calculation of AMP and the related rebate liability for pharmaceutical products. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Federal law also requires that a company that participates in the Medicaid rebate program report ASP information each quarter to CMS for certain categories of drugs that are paid under Part&nbsp;B of the Medicare program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Manufacturers calculate ASP based on a statutorily defined formula and interpretations of the statute by CMS.&nbsp;&nbsp;CMS uses these submissions to determine payment rates for drugs under Medicare Part&nbsp;B and the resulting Medicare payment rate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">Beginning April&nbsp;1, 2013, Medicare payments for all items and services, including drugs and biologics, were reduced by 2% under the sequestration (i.e., automatic spending reductions) required by the Budget Control Act of 2011, as amended by the American Taxpayer Relief Act of 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent legislation extended the 2% reduction, on average, to 2027.&nbsp;&nbsp;This </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">22</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:9.5pt;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">may cause Medicare Part&nbsp;D plans to seek lower prices from manufacturers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Other legislative or regulatory cost containment provisions, as described below, could have a similar effect.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The containment of healthcare costs has become a priority of federal, state and foreign governments, and the prices of drugs have been a focus in this effort.&nbsp;&nbsp;Government healthcare programs and other third-party payors are increasingly&nbsp;challenging the prices charged for medical products and services and examining the medical necessity and cost-effectiveness of medical products and services, in addition to their safety and efficacy.&nbsp;&nbsp;If these payors do not consider our products to be cost-effective compared to other available therapies, they may not cover our products after approval as a benefit under their plans or, if they do, the level of payment may not be sufficient to allow us to sell our products at a profit.&nbsp;&nbsp;The U.S. government, state legislatures and foreign governments also have shown significant interest in implementing cost-containment programs to limit the growth of government-paid healthcare costs, including price controls, restrictions on reimbursement and requirements for substitution of generic products for branded prescription drugs.&nbsp; Certain states have enacted legislation with the goal of controlling prices on branded prescription drugs and placing restrictions on price increases, the effect of which is unknown.&nbsp;&nbsp;Adoption of such controls and measures, and tightening of restrictive policies in jurisdictions with existing controls and measures, could limit payments for products such as ZEJULA, VARUBI, and any other product candidates that we are developing and could adversely affect our net revenues and operating results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">The marketability of ZEJULA, VARUBI, and any other products for which we receive regulatory approval for commercial sale may suffer if the government and third-party payors fail to provide adequate coverage and reimbursement.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, emphasis on managed care in the United States has increased and we expect will continue to increase the pressure on drug pricing.&nbsp;&nbsp;Coverage policies, third-party reimbursement rates and drug pricing regulation may change at any time.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">In the United States, most outpatient prescription drugs may be covered under Medicare Part&nbsp;D.&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicare Part&nbsp;D is a voluntary prescription drug benefit, through which Medicare beneficiaries may enroll in prescription drug plans offered by private entities for coverage of outpatient prescription drugs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Part&nbsp;D plans include both stand-alone prescription drug benefit plans and prescription drug coverage as a supplement to Medicare Advantage plans provided for under Medicare Part&nbsp;C.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9.5pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
